title: This Monkey Climbs Higher in Winter, Up Where Snow Covers Everything
subject: Yunnan snub-nosed monkey

scenes.text: Winter hits. Every other monkey is gone. This one climbs higher, into the snow.
It's the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey, the highest-living primate on Earth. It has been recorded at 4,700 meters.
That's about 15,400 feet, where the ground stays frozen for roughly 280 days a year.
Climbing higher into the cold seems backwards. The reason is the sun.
Up there, stronger sunlight melts fresh snow faster and exposes the lichen the monkeys eat. Their dark fur soaks up the heat.
Fewer than 2,000 remain. A monkey that lives in snow, and the cold is not what threatens it.

description:
The Yunnan snub-nosed monkey climbs higher in winter, up to 4,700 meters.
Strong sunlight melts the snow off its lichen food, and its dark fur absorbs the warmth.
